history.summary: The Peshwa-era temple complex atop Parvati Hill was built by Balaji Baji Rao (Nana Saheb Peshwa) to fulfil his mother Kashibai's vow after she was cured of a foot ailment at the hilltop shrine. The main temple, Devdeveshwar (meaning 'Lord of Lords'), was completed in 1749 with a gold pinnacle added in 1760; it was originally the private shrine of the Peshwa rulers. The complex also houses shrines to Vitthal-Rukmini, Vishnu and Kartikeya, the Peshwa Museum (in the 1795 Peshwa Palace section), and a memorial to Nana Saheb, who preferred living in the temple when seriously ill.

name: Parvati Hill Temple
town_description: Parvati Hill is a 2,100-ft (640 m) hillock in southern Pune, the city's second-highest point and an observation point with 360-degree panoramic views; it is also home to the Peshwa Museum.
tradition: Shaivism (Shiva-Parvati focus, with Vaishnavite shrines in the complex)

travel.road: Drive to the base at Parvati Darshan, then climb 103 stone steps (108 per some sources - verify) to the summit; no entry fee

visitor_information.best_time: October to March; sunrise and sunset for views
visitor_information.opening_hours: 5:00 AM to 8:00 PM daily (entry free); Peshwa Museum has separate hours
